items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We had a nice lunch in the garden of the African cultural center with Mr. and Mrs. Pango

ctx.x: Monsieur Pango has a brother who is a Catholic Priest and a very amazing man. He is also a fine musician. His name is Father Pierre-Michel Pango and he lived in Bingerville. He composed the National anthem of the country which is titled "l'Abidjanaise", when the Ivory Coast got it's independence from France. He directed choirs in Europe and has written many songs and religious compositions. He teaches children and directs a choir in Bingerville, which is a town a few miles from Abidjan.

My last concert was in Bingerville on Sunday the 28th. We had a nice lunch in the garden of the African cultural center with Mr. and Mrs. Pango, some of their eleven children, and Mr Pango's assistant-Mr. "Bill" Yappi. About five, we arrived in Bingerville. The concert had been arranged in the afternoon, so that the kids of the village could attend, and it was the largest crowd of the three concerts. It was open air and the weather was fair. There were hundred of kids, if not thousands, and thousands of adults…
But the crowd at Bingerville topped many of the festivals, I've played in Europe as far as attendance is concerned.
